issues.display_title: Issue #1768: [Editor] Polish the Add New button and sidebar tab bar
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Tidy up two controls at the top of the editor sidebar: the "Add New" button that starts every panel, and the tab bar above it.

Add New button

The button sits at the top of Artworks, Objects, and Text. It kept its familiar look — full width, dashed outline, label with a plus on the right — but a few things were off:

  • It ran flush against both edges of the sidebar. It now sits inset with a little breathing room above it.
  • Its label and plus icon were nudged into place by hand rather than simply centred, so they could drift.
  • Pressing it gave no feedback, and a disabled button looked much the same as an active one.
  • The focus outline appeared on ordinary mouse clicks, not just keyboard navigation.

Tab bar

Artworks, Objects, Text, Settings, and Publish.

  • Hovering an inactive tab only changed the text colour, which was easy to miss in a dense panel. Inactive tabs now get a background tint on hover.
  • Hovering the active tab turned its label dark against its coloured fill. It now keeps its light label.
  • Tabs now respond visibly when pressed.
  • Tabs were built as links even though they don't navigate anywhere. They are now buttons, and each one announces whether it is the current tab, so screen readers and keyboard users get the right behaviour.

Also

The "Set Animation Sequence" row under the Artworks button had uneven spacing; its padding now lines up with the button above it.

Not included

  • No change to what any of these controls do.
  • No backend, API, or data model changes.

Checks

  • Add New works in Artworks, Objects, and Text, including the "Creating text…" state.
  • All five tabs still switch panels.
  • Tabs reachable and operable by keyboard, with a visible focus ring.
  • Active tab label stays legible on hover.
  • Looks right in both light and dark themes.
  • Development build passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1769: [Editor] Match the media support upload row to the Add New button and title field
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Bring the "media support" row under an artwork — the control that attaches a video or audio file to Artwork Info — in line with the rest of the editor sidebar.

Upload control

Before a file is attached, the row showed a link-styled label inside a dashed box: primary colour, underlined on hover, nothing like the other panel actions.

  • It is now the same control as the "Add New" button at the top of each panel — full width, dashed outline, muted label, same height, hover and disabled states included.
  • It is a real button instead of a link, so keyboard and screen-reader behaviour matches the other panel actions.
  • A long label truncates with an ellipsis instead of spilling out of the box.

Attached-file row

Once a file is attached, the row shows its name plus edit and delete icons.

  • The row keeps the same box as the Add New button, so both states line up.
  • The name field is now styled like the exhibition title field at the top of the sidebar: transparent, tinted on hover, focus ring on keyboard focus, ellipsis when the name is long.
  • Edit and delete icons became evenly sized square hit areas with a hover tint, instead of hand-tuned margins.

Not included

  • No change to upload, rename, or delete behaviour — same handlers, same conditions.
  • No backend, API, or data model changes.

Checks

  • Upload opens the file picker; preview dialog and upload still work.
  • Renaming an attached file still saves, and the "Name is required" error still shows.
  • Delete still works, and the spinner still shows while deleting.
  • Controls are disabled while the editor blocks user action.
  • Upload control reachable and operable by keyboard, with a visible focus ring.
  • Looks right in both light and dark themes.
  • Development build passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1770: [Editor] Remove dead Redux state and actions
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Remove Redux slices, actions, and dispatches that have no consumer, while keeping the editor Redux notifications that are still active.

The current Redux store contains unused main and user slices plus editor fields that only receive writes. Keeping them makes the state architecture harder to understand before the editor is migrated to Angular Signals.

Scope

  • Remove the unused Redux main and user slices and their reducer files.
  • Remove the UPDATE_INFO_USER and UPDATE_USER_STORY dispatches from the layout user-loading flow.
  • Keep user profile state flowing through MainService.userInfo and userInfoUpdated.
  • Remove dead editor state and actions:
    • displayDeleteExhibition
    • validateData
    • UPDATE_DELETE_EXIHINITION_STAT
    • VALIDATE_DATA
  • Remove their dispatch call sites and the unused publish-tab delete helper.
  • Preserve the Redux root shape as { editor } so existing redux-watch('editor.*') paths remain compatible.
  • Preserve active editor state:
    • objectHasSelected
    • undoRedo
    • updateObjectData

Out of scope

  • Migrating active editor state to Angular Signals.
  • Fixing reducer immutability.
  • Removing redux or redux-watch dependencies.
  • Changing Babylon.js runtime or lifecycle behavior.

Acceptance criteria

  • Redux root state contains only the editor slice.
  • The editor slice contains only objectHasSelected, undoRedo, and updateObjectData.
  • No references remain to the removed reducers, actions, or state fields.
  • User profile loading and editor selection/undo-redo behavior remain unchanged.
  • The delete-gallery dialog still opens from the editor toolbar and deletion still works.
  • Focused Redux and layout tests pass.
  • The required development build passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1772: [Editor] Introduce EditorSessionStore with Angular Signals
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Introduce a feature-focused Angular Signals store for serializable editor session state. This creates the target state boundary before active Redux notifications are migrated.

Scope

  • Add an injectable EditorSessionStore for editor UI and domain state that belongs to Angular.
  • Keep writable signals private and expose readonly signals and computed state.
  • Define typed editor state for active tab, selection identity, saving/blocking flags, and serializable session metadata needed by later migration issues.
  • Provide explicit mutation methods instead of exposing writable signals.
  • Keep Babylon.js objects such as Engine, Scene, meshes, materials, gizmos, and vectors outside the store.
  • Add focused unit tests for initial state, mutations, readonly exposure, and computed state.

Out of scope

  • Replacing existing Redux watchers.
  • Moving live Babylon.js objects into Signals.
  • Migrating undo/redo or changing editor behavior.
  • Removing Redux dependencies.

Acceptance criteria

  • A typed EditorSessionStore exists and can be injected by editor code.
  • Consumers cannot mutate exposed signals directly.
  • No Babylon.js runtime object is stored in the Signals state.
  • Existing editor behavior remains unchanged.
  • Store unit tests pass.
  • The required development build passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1773: [Editor] Migrate selection and active-tab state to Angular Signals
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Move editor selection and active-tab state from mutable service fields and Redux notifications into EditorSessionStore.

Scope

  • Represent selection as a typed serializable identity: entity kind plus ID, or null.
  • Move active tab state into the Signals store.
  • Update selection/unselection flows to mutate the store through explicit methods.
  • Update Artworks, Objects, Text, Settings, and Publish tab consumers to read signal state.
  • Derive hasSelection from selection instead of maintaining a separate boolean.
  • Keep active Babylon mesh/node references in the Babylon runtime layer during this migration.
  • Remove objectHasSelected Redux state, action dispatches, and watchers once all consumers have moved.

Out of scope

  • Migrating undo/redo and object-update notifications.
  • Moving Babylon nodes or transforms into Signals.
  • Removing Redux entirely.

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting artwork, object, or text updates the typed signal selection.
  • Unselecting clears selection and dependent UI.
  • Single and multi-selection behavior remains unchanged.
  • Tab switching and automatic tab selection remain unchanged.
  • No editor.objectHasSelected Redux references remain.
  • Focused tests and the required development build pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #1774: [Editor] Replace Redux editor notifications with Angular Signals
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Replace Redux timestamp/event-bus notifications for object updates and undo/redo refreshes with Angular Signals.

Scope

  • Replace updateObjectData and undoRedo Redux fields with explicit Signals-based change notifications.
  • Migrate every remaining redux-watch subscription to signal-aware consumption.
  • Remove manual Redux unsubscribe bookkeeping made obsolete by Angular signal lifecycle handling.
  • Preserve component refresh behavior after transform changes, selection restoration, and undo/redo.
  • Prefer meaningful counters or typed event payloads over Date.now() timestamps.
  • Remove migrated Redux actions and reducer fields after the final consumer is converted.

Out of scope

  • Reworking the undo/redo snapshot algorithm.
  • Moving Babylon.js objects into Signals.
  • Removing Redux packages until no consumer remains.

Acceptance criteria

  • Object detail controls refresh after Babylon transform/data updates.
  • General, Publish, Objects, Artwork, and Text controls refresh after undo/redo.
  • No redux-watch imports or store.subscribe calls remain in editor components.
  • No updateObjectData or undoRedo Redux state remains.
  • Focused component/store tests pass.
  • The required development build passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1775: [Editor] Integrate Angular Signals with undo-redo history
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Make undo/redo restore serializable editor state through the Signals store while Babylon.js remains an imperative projection of the restored snapshot.

Scope

  • Define the serializable snapshot boundary for artworks, ordinary objects, text walls, exhibition settings, and camera data.
  • Restore the domain snapshot first, then reconcile the Babylon scene from that restored data.
  • Expose undo/redo availability and in-progress state as derived or readonly Signals.
  • Ensure selection and active controls are reconciled after a restore.
  • Keep history entries free of Babylon.js runtime objects.
  • Preserve existing debounce, invalid-state cleanup, and save-history behavior unless a change is required for correctness.
  • Add tests covering undo, redo, branch truncation after a new edit, and selection reconciliation.

Out of scope

  • Collaborative editing or event sourcing.
  • Persisting history across browser sessions.
  • Replacing Babylon.js rendering.

Acceptance criteria

  • Undo and redo restore matching serializable editor and Babylon scene state.
  • Undo/redo buttons expose correct enabled and busy states.
  • A new edit after undo removes the stale redo branch.
  • History snapshots contain no Babylon.js runtime objects.
  • Existing save and validation workflows remain unchanged.
  • Focused tests and the required development build pass.
